doc: Scenarios for scripts/prompt_loop.py. Each key (except _README) is a
scenario: {intent: 'triage'|'build', entity?: '<record IRI>', turns: [user msgs]}.
Each string in `turns` is one conversation turn (multi-turn = list of >1).
Run one:   prompt_loop.py --file scripts/scenarios.json --scenario ip_triage
Run all:   prompt_loop.py --file scripts/scenarios.json --all
With push: add --push to deploy.sh --bump patch ONCE before the run.
FULL build->see->run proof (drive turns -> accept offer -> push -> verify
in FortiSOAR -> trigger & poll to finished, exit 0 only if all pass):
build_run_proof.py --file scripts/scenarios.json --scenario enrich_then_build
Use a scenario whose LAST turn asks to SAVE/build a playbook (so the agent
emits a playbook_offer card). enrich_then_build is the canonical one.
Override:  --entity <IRI> / --intent <triage|build> override the scenario.
EDIT the `entity` IRIs to records that exist on your box. `null` = no record
context (the agent works from the prompt text alone). Find a live incident:
GET /api/3/incidents?$limit=1&$orderby=-createDate

turns: Triage this incident. Pull the SIEM events, pivot on every external IP you find, and enrich them. Summarize the verdict.
Investigate the host(s) in this incident. Pull each host's recent FortiSIEM activity and any related alerts, then tell me if it looks compromised.
look up ip 87.224.7.73 and tell me if it's malicious
Design a re-runnable FortiSOAR playbook that automates that IP enrichment and parameterize it so it re-runs on similar cases. Produce the playbook YAML.
Triage this incident, and if any external IP is malicious, stage a FortiGate block for it (do not execute — just prepare the action card with the correct parameters).
Triage this incident. Look up the external destination IP from the record and tell me if it's malicious.
Save this investigation as a re-runnable playbook that re-runs on any incident — pull the IP from the triggering record, not a fixed value.
Use FortiSIEM to find any events in the last 24h involving source IP 10.50.60.70, then pivot to its destinations and summarize what you see.
Identify the user account associated with this incident, pull its recent FortiSIEM activity, and check whether it has sessions from other hosts or unusual locations.

doc: interleave_triage_author_enhance is the Phase-0 oracle arc (state-derived-
intent-and-tool-slicing plan): ONE session that crosses triage -> hunt ->
author -> record-edit -> enhance. Under the current single-intent LATCH no
run can serve the whole arc — the deterministic proof is
tests/test_interleave_oracle.py. Driving this scenario with a real model
(--llm frank) is the live counterpart: the agent narrates toward authoring
at turn 3 but the triage-latched slice withholds compile/verify/offer, and
the enhance turn withholds the enhance write pair. `intent` is triage
because the widget is mounted on an incident (the page prior).

turns: Triage this incident: pull the external destination IP from the record and tell me if it's malicious.
Hunt the host involved — pull its recent FortiSIEM activity and any related alerts.
Now author a re-runnable FortiSOAR playbook that automates this IP enrichment, parameterized off the triggering record. Produce the YAML.
Actually, change this incident's type to Phishing first.
Good. Now enhance that playbook: add a step that also enriches the host, and re-verify it.
